definition: A primary reinforcer is a reward that has inherent value rather than needing to be learned, such as sweetness. In learning, it can be used to strengthen responses or to give positive value to another stimulus through conditioning.

reasons: The packet only states that “primary reinforcer (sweetness)” was used as the unconditioned stimulus; it does not support the claim that primary reinforcers have “inherent value rather than needing to be learned.”

The definition claims primary reinforcers can be used “to strengthen responses” and “to give positive value to another stimulus through conditioning,” but the packet does not make those general statements about the function of primary reinforcers beyond describing their use in an evaluative conditioning procedure.
The phrase about using a primary reinforcer to “strengthen responses” is not supported by the packet.
